summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the medicine service for weeks of intermittent post-prandial confusion and concern for hypoglycemia and malabsorption. Initial evaluation showed normal CBC, chemistries, and liver tests with low/normal ammonia; endocrinology supervised an overnight fast with tube feeds held, during which she did not become hypoglycemic, and fasting insulin/C-peptide/beta-hydroxybutyrate were within normal limits with proinsulin pending. Hepatology felt her episodes were not due to hepatic encephalopathy or cirrhosis; after a monitored high-protein meal she developed transient slurred speech and tremor with subsequent amnesia and post-meal rises in transaminases/albumin, raising concern for a possible urea cycle/metabolic contribution, and a urea cycle panel was sent (pending). EEG and brain MRI were normal. She was discharged home ambulatory with instructions to continue continuous tube feeds (transitioning to NutriHep when available), avoid oral caloric intake except water, continue rifaximin, hold atenolol given bradycardia, and follow up outpatient to review pending results and ongoing management of post-gastric surgery symptoms and hypoglycemia.
problems: Other complications of other bariatric procedure
